title: SignalForge onboarding ramp + SLA alignment
summary: Introductory implementation kick-off for SignalForge. Discussed security constraints (data residency, KMS, SOC2), deployment modes, SLA/latency targets, pilot scope (30k daily tokens), and next steps including benchmark run and pricing options. Action items assigned for a follow up demo and security packet.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share dedicated vs hosted pricing sheet and a one-page pilot SOW - due 2026-09-08
Liam O'Neal: Provision benchmark test harness and sample prompt set; run baseline latency tests on 2 model variants - due 2026-09-10
Sofia Martinez: Provide data residency requirements, KMS key policy, and SOC2 point of contact - due 2026-09-07
Tom Ellis: Share current network topology diagram and IP allowlist requirements for VPC peering - due 2026-09-09
next_steps: Send security packet and SOC2 / ISO docs via secure link
Agree on pilot success criteria and accept test prompts
Maya to propose pilot SOW and pricing by 2026-09-08
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-04 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 56m | Recording started
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (CTO, SignalForge), Daniel Park (Head of MLOps), Sofia Martinez (IT Security), Tom Ellis (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick round robin — we got the core team on the call. i'll let aisha intro for a sec.
[00:18] Aisha: yeah hi all, thanks. we're kicking off the onboarding for our customer support assistant project. timeline is tight — q4 rollout ideally. daniel, you wanna add?
[00:26] Daniel: sure, thanks. main goals are conversational routing and ticket summarization. currently running on GCP, k8s, mostly private clusters. latency target for user-facing flow is sub 300ms tail if possible.
[00:38] Liam: okay sub 300ms tail is ambitious for open models depending on batch and sequence length, we can discuss dedicated capacity and model variants.
[00:48] Sofia: hi — security first question: we need data residency in eu-west-1 for logs and customer data, and our compliance team will require KMS integration and audit logs. are those supported?
[01:02] Maya: yes, we support region pinning and KMS/HSM integrations on private deployments; for hosted we'll need to align on retention windows. i'll follow up with the SOC2 docs.
[01:15] Priya: just to clarify onboarding scope, we propose a 4-week pilot: integration, benchmark, and acceptance tests. is that aligned?
[01:24] Aisha: sounds right, daniel — does that fit your ramp?
[01:28] Daniel: yes, with one caveat — we want to validate both hosted and dedicated flows because cost tradeoffs are material.
[01:36] Maya: understood. we'll show you hosted for quick time-to-value and dedicated for sustained throughput/cost predictability.
[01:44] Tom: network wise, we prefer VPC peering or private link. what's the typical network setup?
[01:52] Liam: we can do VPC peering for private deployments; for hosted we offer a private endpoint option with allowlist. expect some NAT/firewall changes on your side. we'll provide a runbook.
[02:04] Speaker 4: (crosstalk) the IPs — is it a fixed pool?
[02:10] Liam: mostly stable, but i'll send the definitive allowlist. note sometimes ephemeral egress can appear in logs, we document it.
[02:18] Maya: let's jump to pilot success criteria — daniel, what are your KPIs?
[02:24] Daniel: correctness for summarization (ROUGE-ish metric), response latency < 300ms p95 for short prompts, and cost per 1k tokens under our threshold. also operational readiness: rollout automation and model pinning.
[02:38] Liam: for latency, sequence length and batching are the big drivers. we'll instrument KV cache and prefix caching so warm convo flows hit lower latency.
[02:48] Aisha: about data, will any user utterance be persisted in Redwood logs? retention?
[02:54] Priya: retention policy is configurable; hosted defaults to 30 days but we can set it to 0 for no retention on enterprise plans; private no retention unless you opt in.
[03:06] Sofia: need that in writing. auditor will want an explicit statement.
[03:11] Maya: absolutely — security packet forthcoming.

--- Topics: SLA, pilot scope, networking, security, benchmarks ---

[03:25] Liam: i'm gonna walk through a rough topology and the benchmark plan. first, we'll run two model variants: a lighter quantized open model and a larger base with evals. We'll capture p50/p95 token latencies and token cost.
[03:42] Daniel: what's the expected delta between hosted and dedicated throughput?
[03:46] Liam: dedicated gives you more sustained QPS with predictable tail latencies due to reserved GPUs and lower multi-tenant variance. hosted can be bursty but is faster to start. hard numbers depend on model and batch settings; we'll provide sample perf numbers from our catalog.
[04:02] Maya: note also we have automatic fallbacks to smaller model variants if capacity is constrained, which helps maintain availability.
[04:12] Aisha: fallback is fine but need consistent output quality. how do you test regressions?
[04:18] Liam: Redwood Optimize links regressions to prompt sets and monitors quality metrics; we'll run A/B with your prompts during the pilot.
[04:28] Daniel: need a procedure: if quality drops beyond threshold we should auto rollback. is that supported?
[04:34] Liam: yes can be configured — canary rollout with automatic fallback policy.

[04:45] Tom: ops question — what's the auth flow for private? SSO?
[04:50] Priya: we support SAML SSO and RBAC that maps to your IdP groups; we'll share the SSO integration doc.
[04:58] Sofia: encryption-at-rest and in transit — are customer keys supported?
[05:03] Maya: yes customer-managed KMS keys are supported for private installs and optional for hosted enterprise accounts.
[05:10] Sofia: great, we'll send KMS policy.

[05:20] Speaker 2: (mumble) also want to confirm logging — we need to ship audit logs to our ELK stack.
[05:27] Liam: you can configure log forwarding to your S3 or SIEM; for private you get full control.

[05:35] Maya: let's talk timeline. Proposed pilot: week 1 integration and onboarding, week 2 benchmark run, week 3 tuning and regression tests, week 4 acceptance and go/no-go. Any blockers?
[05:48] Aisha: resource availability is the main thing; we'll assign daniel and tom as leads. Sofia will review security artifacts.
[05:56] Daniel: we also want to include a small sample of real prompts — about 500 — for early tuning.
[06:03] Liam: perfect; please share anonymized prompt set and we'll run the eval harness.

[06:12] Maya: pricing question — daniel mentioned cost sensitivity. we'll share per-token examples and a dedicated commit option with discount tiers.
[06:22] Daniel: what about quantized models and unit economics?
[06:26] Liam: quantization can reduce GPU memory and cost; for some workflows quality is nearly identical, for others you may see small deltas. Our Optimize tool suggests quant profiles per workload.
[06:40] Aisha: okay remind me on support SLAs — response times for Sev1?
[06:45] Priya: enterprise customers get 1-hour Sev1 response and 24x7 escalation. we'll include that in the SOW.

[06:54] Sofia: auditor question — do you have a customer-managed attestation flow for data deletion?
[07:00] Maya: yes we document deletion APIs and can provide an attestation report for the pilot.

[07:08] Tom: about networking — do you require VPN or peering for private?
[07:12] Liam: peering preferred; VPN is possible but adds latency and complexity. we'll provide the runbook with CIDR ranges.

[07:22] Speaker 1: (laughs) okay lots of homework.

[07:26] Maya: recap: Redwood will send pricing, security packet, allowlist and runbook. we'll schedule the benchmark next week. Customer to send prompts, KMS policy, and network diagram.
[07:38] Aisha: thanks team. one more thing — timeline: can we start integration work by 9/13?
[07:44] Maya: yes, if we lock SOW by 9/10. We'll aim for that.

[07:50] Daniel: for bench — can you run both hosted and dedicated flows in parallel so we can see delta?
[07:55] Liam: yes, we'll stand up parallel runs and annotate cost data.

[08:03] Sofia: send the SOC2 and ISO docs to our secure drop and cc our legal.
[08:08] Maya: will do.

[08:12] Priya: action items and owners will be in the calendar invite follow-up.

[08:18] Maya: any final Qs?
[08:21] Tom: none from me.
[08:23] Aisha: nope thanks.

[08:26] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up this afternoon with the security packet and pricing.

[08:30] (end)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and ambient cross-talk; some acronyms transcribed as separate letters (e.g., K V cache).

Recap (as read back):
- Pilot: 4-week plan covering integration, bench, tuning, and acceptance.
- Security: KMS, SOC2 docs, data residency (eu-west-1), audit logs and deletion APIs required.
- Networking: prefer VPC peering, provide allowlist and runbook.
- Bench: run hosted + dedicated variants, capture p50/p95 latencies and cost per 1k tokens, use 500 sample prompts.
- Next steps: Maya to send pricing and SOW; Liam to prepare benchmark harness; customer to send prompts, KMS policy, and network diagram.

End of recording.
